title: Quantized-Fallback Quality SLA and Rollout Spec
author: Priya Anand
summary: This document defines production quality objectives, telemetry, and an operational rollout & fallback procedure for deploying quantized model variants. It describes deterministic checks, signal thresholds, routing matrix, and an investigation/rollback playbook to ensure production quality is maintained when we serve mixed-precision or INT8/FP16 variants alongside float baselines.
background: Redwood routinely deploys quantized model variants to reduce cost and improve throughput. Quantized variants can introduce subtle output degradation or distributional shifts that only appear under certain workloads (long context, streaming function calls, or rare tokens). This spec formalizes acceptance criteria, automated fallback routing, and a staged rollout protocol so product codepaths experience low risk during quantized rollouts.
scope: Applies to all model promotions where a quantized serving variant is introduced into production routing (hosted, dedicated, or private). Includes changes that affect kernel selection, KV cache behavior, and prefix caching semantics. Excludes research experiments gated behind feature flags (those live in experimental sandboxes).
definitions:
- Float baseline: The production float (FP32/FP16) model variant we consider the quality reference.
- Quant variant: Any quantized model variant (INT8, INT8+PTQ, hybrid mixed-precision) intended for serving.
- Quality-critical route: API routes marked with 'quality:critical' in the console (e.g., chat generation, legal summarization).
- SLO breach: Metric crossing threshold for more than the configured rollout interval (see SLO windows below).
quality_slos:
Primary SLOs for quantized variants compared versus float baseline over the canary window (typically 24h):

1) Semantic fidelity (primary): meanSemanticDelta <= 0.015 absolute (derived from a weighted semantic-similarity metric combining embedding cosine and normalized token overlap).
   - Measurement: 10k stratified probes representative of production slices (multi-turn, long-context, high-entropy queries).
2) Latency: p95 tail increase <= 15% vs baseline for same traffic slice. Absolute p95 must remain < 1200ms for hosted small models, < 250ms for low-latency routes.
3) Error surface: functional error rate (exceptions, truncated streams, invalid JSON in structured outputs) <= baseline + 0.01 (1 percentage point).
4) Regression budget: no more than 2 significant semantic regressions in critical prompt slices (defined in prompt coverage matrix) during the 24h canary.

Notes: All comparisons use production-weighted sampling; if sample size < 1k in the window use the extended window (72h) before decision.
acceptance_checks:
Automated checks to run before traffic is routed: 
- Deterministic unit tests: tokenization parity, KV cache correctness, logits shape checks.
- Shadow replay: 1000 previously logged requests replayed through quant variant and compared to baseline using similarity metric; fail if meanSemanticDelta > 0.02.
- Slice smoke: Run the top 50 heuristic prompt slices (from prompt-sets-and-benchmarks) against quant variant; flag any slice with delta > 0.03.
- Resource sanity: GPU memory and peak utilization within expected bounds (no >10% overcommit vs simulated load).
fallback_routing_matrix:
Routing is controlled by two orthogonal axes: traffic fraction and route criticality. Matrix: 

- Quality-critical routes:
  - Stage 0: shadow-only.
  - Stage 1: 1% traffic, strict monitoring, immediate fallback if any critical slice breaches.
  - Stage 2: 5% traffic after 24h stable.
  - Stage 3: 20% traffic gated on 72h stability and manual review.
  - Stage 4: full traffic only after a rollout sign-off.

- Non-critical bulk routes:
  - Stage 0: shadow-only.
  - Stage 1: 5% traffic, automated rollback guard.
  - Stage 2: 50% if 48h stable.
  - Stage 3: 100% after 7d and periodic audits.

Fallback behavior: requests routed back to float baseline if either: (a) p95 latency breach for the route exceeds threshold for 5 consecutive 10-minute buckets; or (b) semantic delta on a stratified slice exceeds the SLO and persists for two sampling intervals. Fallback is applied at the route level and propagated to downstream caches and CDN edge configs.
rollout_procedure:
Step-by-step rollout checklist:

1) Pre-rollout (owners: model-onboarding + runtime):
   - Create rollout ticket with model variant id, quant profile, and rollout window.
   - Attach probe set id and slice coverage matrix.
   - Run acceptance_checks in CI with debug logging enabled.

2) Shadow validation (owners: eval-harness):
   - Shadow 72h of live traffic or replay a representative corpus; collect similarity metrics and error logs.
   - Run 'smoke & slice' sweep.

3) Canary ingress (owners: eng-platform):
   - Configure routing rule with traffic fraction per fallback_routing_matrix.
   - Enable telemetry dashboards and anomaly detectors specific to quant signals (latency, semantic delta, structured-output mismatch).

4) Monitoring window (owners: SRE + applied-ml):
   - Observe first 2h for infra regressions, then 24h for quality metrics.
   - Use automatic alerting to notify on-call if any SLO breaches.

5) Scale up / sign-off (owners: product + applied-ml):
   - If stable, increase to next stage per matrix. Document manual approvals in rollout ticket.

6) Post-rollout audit:
   - Run a 7-day audit comparing production-weighted metrics, and add findings to the model's promotion record.
telemetry_and_alerting:
Core telemetry to surface:
- semantic.delta.mean, semantic.delta.p95 (by slice and overall)
- latency.p50/p95/p99 (by model and route)
- structured-output.validation.fail_rate (JSON schema checks for function calls)
- tokenization.mismatch.count
- resource.memory.peak and gpu_utilization.percent

Alert rules (examples):
- P1: semantic.delta.mean > 0.02 for any quality-critical slice for two consecutive 15-minute windows -> Pager to on-call applied-ml + SRE.
- P1: structured-output.fail_rate > baseline + 0.02 -> immediate rollback unless sign-off.
- P2: latency.p95 increased > 20% for route -> Slack alert to owning team.

Instrumentation notes: label all metrics with model_variant, quant_profile, route, and rollout_ticket_id. Use the eval-harness job id as a tag to link shadow runs back to production metrics.
investigation_and_rollback_playbook:
If an alert triggers: 
1) Triage (first 15 minutes):
   - Owner inspects dashboards, checks recent kernel/compilation changes, and looks for config drift.
   - Run deterministic repro: replay failing slice with identical headers and tokens.
2) Quick mitigations (15-60 minutes):
   - If infra-related (OOMs, kernel failures), scale down quant variant traffic and apply static resource limits.
   - If quality-related, trigger automated route-level fallback and capture a forensics bundle (10k samples, token-level diffs).
3) Deeper analysis (60-240 minutes):
   - Apply bisect: compare baseline -> quant-lite -> quant-full to isolate the change.
   - Use eval-harness to run differential logging including logits drift, top-k token shifts, and attention-pattern divergence.
4) Postmortem and mitigation:
   - Owners produce a 72h incident notes doc with root cause, remediation, and rollout policy updates.
   - Update quant profiles or rollback to previous quant variant; codify any new acceptance test.
example_config_snippets:
YAML example for route config: 

route: /v1/generate-chat
model_variant: my-model-v3-int8
quant_profile: int8-ptq-v2
rollout_ticket_id: ROLLOUT-2026-213
traffic_rules:
  - stage: 1
    fraction: 0.01
    duration_hours: 24
    monitors: [semantic.delta, latency.p95, structured-output.fail_rate]
  - stage: 2
    fraction: 0.05
    duration_hours: 24

SDK snippet (curl):
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/routing/set -d '{"route":"/v1/generate-chat","model_variant":"my-model-v3-int8","fraction":0.01}' -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>'
